components.name: Music House

reviewers: Astra xhigh builder continuation: all seven actual PNGs and all four source originals inspected
root independent native review: all seven actual PNGs inspected; bounded verdict agreed
findings: One continuous glazed gable is registered to the measured link crown; the former rectangular pale perimeter beam and duplicate roof are absent.

Gray panes and sparse black pane divisions replace the bright iron lattice. The front and side-return corner are visibly connected, with occupied heads and sills; no new daylight slit is visible in the inspected close views.
Both modern flank panels have continuous pale quartz-brick spandrels instead of brown belts. The source panel hierarchy is restored although the top/sill profiles remain coarse.
The three historic doors now have connected stepped pointed surrounds around visibly peaked dark apertures. Their carving, finials and inscriptions remain simplified.

The three west dormer windows sit lower within the retained roof bounds, leaving readable brick triangles. Five authored historic cross gables remain distinct; no measured roof ridge was raised for this correction.
Both historic bays are shallow deliberate curved approximations, joined to their straight host planes. Their pane corners and sill/head returns are occupied in the close bay view.
The east-end 6/6/2 light schedule is centered under its measured ridge. The measured rear inset is retained, and the exposed foundation follows the falling grade.
Long facade runs remain consistent planes with regular orientation steps and the real west-wing bend. The rear grade view retains an exposed lower storey and conservative repeated openings.

Exact archive-to-Anvil parity and native provenance pass for all 2487049 occupied states; zero missing, extra or mismatched states and no forbidden materials. Physical audits pass for 2691 panes, 967 partial backing records and eight operable door leaves.
verdict.acceptance_boundary: Bounded visible exterior improvement over rejected v6, suitable to replace the measured Quadrivium shell in a fresh campus assembly. This does not certify complete photographic likeness, unseen elevations, interiors, site completion or the combined campus; campus context requires its own review.
remaining_limitations: At two blocks per metre the limestone surrounds, stepped arches and bay curves remain thick and angular; exact carving, sash subdivision, inscriptions and finials are unresolved.

The pale modern side-panel spandrels read as stacked rails in close views because occupied sill/head backing and half-metre courses compress the field; material continuity is corrected but the source flatness is only approximate.
Dormer triangles are improved within fixed roof limits but retain asymmetric grid steps and exaggerated pale trim at some corners.

Historic slate and the pale metal crown use vanilla stone-brick and smooth-quartz appearance proxies. Retained measured roof samples create local ridge/eave irregularities, including the east-end top; no unsupported whole-roof smoothing is claimed.
Rear opening rows remain inferred and the large modern rear wall remains a conservative measured mass, not a verified photographed facade.
The east lower-grade black railing is not yet modeled; local landscape, planting, approach finish and pavement raster detail are incomplete.
Pane tint denotes a source-matched appearance proxy, not evidence that the real building uses literally gray or black glass. Interior floor edges are visible through the glazing.

Photo opening registration and authored dormer/portal controls remain interpreted. Source exceptions retain the photographed upper frontage over the anomalously low source face and the tall modern flank over its low slate return.
